thread:
diego_oncall: heads-up — getting a customer escalation: their p99 is spiking to ~12s on /v1/generate (Dedicated pool). They reported a few 504s. Happened after last night's autoscale config change (reduced overprovision). Can someone triage?

carla_support: customer org id: org_9XJ. Symptoms: requests queue timeouts, long attach times. Repro steps they gave: steady rps ~30 with bursts to 120, most requests are ~1k tokens. They see p95 ~800ms, p99 ~12s for last 30m.

diego_oncall: adding logs and metrics I pulled:

autoscale-bot: autoscale events (last 45m):
```
[1745601000] scale_request pool=dedicated-prod-3 delta=+8 reason=burst
[1745601080] attach_start pool=dedicated-prod-3 job=attach-546a
[1745601150] attach_timeout pool=dedicated-prod-3 job=attach-546a
[1745601180] scale_request pool=dedicated-prod-3 delta=+16 reason=queued
[1745601220] attach_success pool=dedicated-prod-3 job=attach-547b elapsed=64s
```

ben_sre: attach elapsed 64s is the problem — looks like cold-GPU attach latency. Did the recent change reduce warm pool capacity?

alice_eng_runtime: yes, last-night change reduced warm buffer from 20% -> 5% to save cost. That increased cold starts under burst. For this workload 1k tokens, kernel selection time + model load is ~30-45s. With container handshake and networking it's hitting 60s.

marie_prod: customer is hitting SLOs. They want ETA to mitigate. Can we do a quick mitigation before full rollback?

ben_sre: short-term mitigations: 1) temporarily increase warm buffer to 25% for dedicated-prod-3, 2) raise max parallel attach threads on attacher from 10 -> 30, 3) enable fast-fallback routing to a smaller quantized model if attach latency > 5s. Any objections?

carla_support: prefer option 1 + 3. Option 2 might overload attacher if we don't also increase host capacity.

alice_eng_runtime: I can push warm buffer bump now. Command:
```
# increase warm buffer for pool
rdwctl pool update dedicated-prod-3 --warm-buffer 0.25 --reason "hotfix: customer p99 spike"
```

alice_eng_runtime: and enable fallback routing rule:
```
rdwctl routing add-rule --name fast-fallback-quantized --if "attach_time > 5000" --to model:llama-q4b
```

autoscale-bot: action applied: pool_update accepted (req 8243) — warm-buffer -> 0.25. routing-rule created id=fast-fallback-202403.

ben_sre: monitoring p95/p99 now. Watch attach queue length and GPU utilization. If attach queue grows, revert increase to attacher parallelism only after adding more attacher worker nodes.

diego_oncall: digging into attacher logs: I see repeated "model load OOM" warnings for some jobs which then fallback to a different instance type. That slowed attach pipeline. Example log:
```
[1745601102] attach-546a ERROR model_load OOM model=redwood-v1-13B quantized=false mem_req=31GB avail=28GB
[1745601110] attach-546a WARN fallback to node-type=gpu-p4d-8x
```

alice_eng_runtime: that suggests node sizing mismatch for large models. For immediate relief, we can preferentially schedule big-model attaches to nodes with >32GB GPU memory and schedule smaller models to p4d. Will update pool placement.

ben_sre: agree. Also recommend temporarily increasing attach timeout threshold from 60s -> 120s to avoid client 504s while we stabilize. We should notify API gateway to extend timeout for this pool.

carla_support: message drafted to customer (waiting approval): "We're seeing transient infrastructure cold starts after a config change; we've temporarily increased warm capacity and enabled a fast-fallback to a quantized model to reduce tail latency. We will keep you posted and can open a dedicated call. Apologies for the disruption." Approve?

marie_prod: lgtm. Send now.

ben_sre: quick checklist for follow-up (assign owners):
- increase warm buffer -> alice_eng_runtime (done)
- enable routing fallback -> alice_eng_runtime (done)
- monitor attach queue & GPU mem OOMs -> diego_oncall
- increase attacher worker nodes if queue > 10 -> infra-oncall (TBD)
- rollback last-night overprovision change if issues persist -> eng-sre lead

alice_eng_runtime: I'm going to patch placement rules to prefer >32GB nodes for big models:
```
rdwctl pool placement update dedicated-prod-3 --rule "model_mem_req >= 30GB -> node_type=gpu-a100-40gb"
```

autoscale-bot: placement update queued (req 8245).

diego_oncall: after warm buffer bump, p99 dropped from 12s -> 1.2s within 7m. Attach queue length down from 18 -> 3. CPU/GPU util normalized. Still seeing occasional OOM fallbacks; watching.

ben_sre: good. Action items: follow up tomorrow to revert customer-visible fallbacks and run a canary for warm-buffer 10% vs 25% with real traffic. Also add a test to our CI that simulates burst attach to gauge warm-buffer needs for different token sizes.

carla_support: customer notified, offered zoom. Customer acknowledged and will monitor.

marie_prod: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will escalate to postmortem if we see recurrence.

diego_oncall: leaving this thread open for 24h. If any regressions, ping here and we'll reopen. Thanks all :thumbsup:
